outcome.technical:
SCOPE GAP FIRST: the hook's marks are dropped on append until plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_journal_io.py DETAILS_KEYS holds `callBegan` and `hookRun`. normalise_details keeps only listed keys, without a word. That file is outside this task's four files and the orchestrator limited me to those four, so I did not edit it. The needed change is to append `, "callBegan", "hookRun"` after `"basis"` in DETAILS_KEYS, plus a comment like the `runId`/`commitNonce` ones: a moment and a random join key, bounded like any value, exposing nothing. Until it lands, two cases in suites outside the task gate are red, honestly: tests/test__journal_io.py dk1 names journal-writes.py:941/942/961/962 callBegan/hookRun, and tests/test_journal_writes.py cm1 reads back rows with no marks. Proof: in a copy of this tree with only that one line added (scratchpad/P142.46-probe/allowlist-copy), test_journal_writes 150/150 and test__journal_io 262/262. The mutation probe applies the same line in its copy as a stated prerequisite. Without it, every new row has no start and gets the reading kept for rows without one, so the fail-open stays open in practice. Fix this before the phase signs off.

CHANGES. journal-writes.py: new `_call_marks(pre, start)` -> (callBegan, hookRun). callBegan is the later of the slot's `ts` (when the baseline bytes were read) and `_config.call_start` (this writer's last sweep-lane PreToolUse, which keeps a slot whose digest still matches). It is floored to the second, the `ts` spelling, and None when neither moment is known. hookRun is os.urandom(8).hex(), one per diff. I did not use the slot's `ts` alone, which is the brief's literal reading: `_pre_seed_sweep` keeps an unmoved slot, so its `ts` can predate the call by many calls, and slots are per writer key. Example: agent B's slot was read at 11:50. A blocks the task at 12:00, an out-of-band move restores in_progress at 12:01, and B's Pre at 12:02 finds the digest equal and keeps the slot. B's row would then carry 11:50 and fold over a real restart. The later of the two moments is never earlier than the last time the baseline was seen standing, and a moment that is too late only stops a fold. `_manifest_rows(..., marks=None)` writes both marks on the edit row and on each derived row; both lanes pass them (`_swept_tree`, `post_rows`). Added `import time`, already loaded by _config. bench-hooks --gate exit 0. audit-task.py: new `_HOOK_BEGAN`/`_HOOK_RUN_ID` and `_call_marks(row)` -> None when details lack callBegan, else (moment or None, run or None). The origin tuple gains marks as a sixth element (`_origin` default widened). New `_one_tree`: same `_journal_io.writer_of` (the session plus worktree key, month stripped). `_echoes` now requires: hook writer, same from/to, same tree. For a marked row: after a named non-hook writer, fold iff callBegan reads and is <= last's stamp; a derived row folds iff it carries the hookRun of the hook edit row before it, regardless of rows between. Rows without callBegan go to `_echoes_unstarted`, which is the previous body verbatim and is named as the reading for rows that carry no start. The comment above the window constants now says the window bounds only rows with no start, is no proof of an echo, and does not count permission waits, MCP calls, a raised Bash cap or the hook's start delay. `_hook_run`'s docstring says it is the adjacency reading for rows without hookRun. Residual, stated in the hook docstring: flooring to the second leaves a fold for a later call whose Pre starts in the verb row's own second after an out-of-band move inside that second. Parallel calls of one writer key overwrite the call-start file, which only overstates (fails closed).
